root_motivation: The sandbox bridge (import mcphost; mcphost.state/table/docs/lineage/call/progress) already exists and works, but no surface a python tool author actually reads names the import -- the 2026-09-30 fleet-board dogfood grounding shows a coder wrote import host, got a bare ModuleNotFoundError traceback, read host.quickstart's own note about persistence with no import name in it, and concluded (wrongly) that the sandbox could not persist state, burning three coder rounds and ~95 tool calls instead of host.quickstart's documented four. This PRD makes every surface a python tool author sees -- quickstart's sandbox_api field, the starter tool, the static/run-time unknown_import checks, tools/list, and the three docs -- name import mcphost from one Rust constant, so the gap can't reopen by a module being added to the runner without that constant following.
user_persona: An integration-specialist/workflow-orchestrator agent (projects/mcp-host.md) publishing its first python tool and needing to persist or read tenant state from inside it, discoverable from host.quickstart alone with no human relay.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a fresh tenant, When it calls host.quickstart kind=python, Then the response carries sandbox_api.import == "import mcphost" and sandbox_api.modules keys exactly equal to the runner script's registered mcphost.* modules, and a fixture that adds a module to the registration constant sees it in quickstart with no other edit.

Given the python starter_tool from quickstart published verbatim, When host.tool_test runs its test_call, Then the result contains a bridge appended count and host.table.query on the starter's table returns the row.

Given a python spec whose source contains import host, When host.spec_test or host.tool_publish runs, Then the error class is unknown_import, data.hint contains import mcphost and all three module names, and nothing is published.

Given a published python tool whose source does import mcphost_sdk inside a function (escaping the static scan), When it is called, Then the call fails unknown_import with the same hint and no raw traceback appears in result.

Given a free-plan tenant, When it calls host.quickstart kind=python, Then limits.plan.network_public names the plan that allows network: "public", and the python row of try_before_call says network is off by default.
Given tools/list, When fetched, Then the host.tool_publish description and the python kind's field help each contain import mcphost and mcphost.table.

Given scripts/sandbox-api-doc-check.sh at the landing commit, When run, Then it exits 0 and reports modules=<n> docs_in_sync=3; given a fixture doc with one module removed, Then it exits 1 naming the missing module and file.

Given the landed binary deployed on prod, When a fresh tenant created by the synthorg explore persona runs host.quickstart kind=python and publishes the returned starter verbatim, Then its first host.tool_test succeeds and host.usage by=tool for that tenant shows at most 6 calls between quickstart and the first successful bridge write (Live: prod tenant, evidence = the probe's JSON report and host.usage output pasted into the PRD's evidence block).

additional.sandbox_api_modules_includes_lineage: AC1 requires sandbox_api.modules keys to exactly equal the runner script's registered mcphost.* modules -- that set is four (state, table, docs, lineage), not the three AC3's own hint-text wording names, so BRIDGE_MODULES and sandbox_api carry all four; AC3's "contains ... all three module names" is satisfied as a subset check (the hint lists all four, which trivially contains any three of them), never read as "contains only three".

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the static import scan (AC3) need a separate run-time ModuleNotFoundError mapping (AC4) at all, instead of just rejecting every disallowed import at publish time?
five_whys_trace.a: The static scan is deliberately a line-based text match over literal import/from statements (the PRD's own Technical considerations: no AST, dynamic imports out of scope) -- a source that builds its import dynamically (importlib.import_module("mcphost_sdk")) never contains a literal import mcphost_sdk line, so it publishes cleanly and only fails once that call actually executes and CPython itself raises ModuleNotFoundError. AC4 exists specifically to give that run-time failure the same unknown_import class and hint instead of leaking a raw exception class/traceback, since the static half can't catch everything by construction.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is BRIDGE_MODULES a hand-written Rust constant kept in sync with PY_RUNNER_SCRIPT's sys.modules[...] lines by a test, rather than generating PY_RUNNER_SCRIPT's own module-registration code from the constant?
five_whys_trace.a: PY_RUNNER_SCRIPT is a single large raw-string Python literal with hand-written request/response plumbing per module (each one's own _state_call/_table_call-style synchronous round trip through the sidecar bridge) -- collapsing that into codegen from a simple (name, signatures) list would be a much larger refactor than this PRD's scope, and isn't what any AC actually requires. AC1 only requires that sandbox_api.modules exactly equal what the runner script registers; runner_script_registered_modules() parses the actual sys.modules[...] lines back out of the script text and a test asserts the two never drift, which proves the invariant without the larger refactor.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the starter tool change (AC2) require editing three already-landed tests from a different PRD (PRD-mcphost-first-publish-real-kind's firstpub_ac01/ac07/ac10)?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 2 explicitly mandates turning host.quickstart's one starter_tool into a bridge example ("the python starter_tool becomes a bridge example ... test_call matches"), which necessarily changes its source, name, and result shape -- the three firstpub_ac* tests pinned the old reversed/words shape byte-for-byte, so leaving them unedited would either fail them outright or (worse) force keeping two different starter tools. Editing a prior PRD's test to match an intentional, later-PRD-mandated change to shared surface is the same pattern this repo already uses elsewhere (e.g. PRD-mcphost-session-bound-tenant-after-signup's own AC12 renames a field a prior test asserted on).

five_whys_trace.q: Why is python_field_hint (previously private to kinds::python, used only for publish-time error messages) now pub(crate) and embedded into handler.rs's tools/list schema instead of writing a second, independent sandbox-API sentence for tools/list?
five_whys_trace.a: AC6 names two places (host.tool_publish's description, and "the python kind's field help ('network' => ... block)") that must each mention import mcphost/mcphost.table -- the second is a direct pointer at this exact match arm's own code locus, matching the PRD's own Grounding-paragraph convention of citing precise source locations. Reusing the same hint text keeps the two in sync by construction (one string, two readers: the invalid_spec error path and tools/list) rather than risking two independently-worded mentions drifting apart.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does scripts/sandbox-api-doc-check.sh parse src/kinds/python.rs's text directly with a regex instead of adding a CLI subcommand that dumps BRIDGE_MODULES as JSON?
five_whys_trace.a: scripts/gen-oauth-scenarios-doc.sh already establishes this repo's convention for a doc-sync script: read the structured source directly (there, a TOML gold file; here, a Rust const's own literal syntax) rather than requiring a compiled binary to introspect itself. A CLI dump subcommand would need a full cargo build before the doc check could ever run, making it unusable as a fast, standalone pre-commit-style check -- the regex (two patterns, name: "..." and purpose: "...", matched in order within the BRIDGE_MODULES block) is simple enough that AC7's own fixture test (one module's bullet line removed) proves it actually detects drift, not just that it runs.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should AC1's sandbox_api.modules list include mcphost.lineage, given AC3's own hint-text wording names only three modules ("mcphost.state, mcphost.table, mcphost.docs")?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes -- AC1's own text requires sandbox_api.modules to exactly equal the runner script's registered mcphost.* modules, which is four (state/table/docs/lineage), not three; AC3's "data.hint contains ... all three module names" is a subset ("contains") requirement, satisfied by a hint that also names a fourth module, never read as "contains exactly three and no more".

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should the starter tool's table be auto-created on first publish, or should quickstart tell the author to run host.table.create first? (PRD's own open question, drafted default: starter calls table.create if missing.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Starter calls mcphost.table.create and catches TableError where .code == "table_already_exists", per the PRD's own stated default -- makes the starter's test_call (and any later real call) idempotent and safe to repeat, matching host.quickstart's own "safe to retry while iterating" convention for every other step.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should mcphost.call (call a sibling tool) appear in the starter as well, or only in sandbox_api.attrs? (PRD's own open question, drafted default: listed in attrs, not in the starter.)
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Listed only in sandbox_api.attrs, per the PRD's own stated default -- the starter's own job (AC2) is proving a bridge write through mcphost.table, and composing a second tool call would widen what test_call has to prove without any AC asking for it.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How should AC4's "a published python tool whose source does import mcphost_sdk inside a function (escaping the static scan)" actually be constructed as a test fixture, given the static scan (as implemented) matches a literal import statement regardless of indentation?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Via importlib.import_module("mcphost_sdk") -- a dynamic call, not a literal import statement -- which the static scan's own text-matching design (no AST, literal import/from lines only) cannot catch by construction, matching requirement 3's own "dynamic imports are out of scope" carve-out and making the AC4 fixture a genuine escape rather than an artifact of under-scanning indented lines.
